subject: Recap & next steps: Data segregation requirements for Dedicated vs VPC
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: Data segregation requirements for Dedicated vs VPC

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the call today — good conversation. I wanted to capture what I heard and propose immediate next steps so we can move toward a clear recommendation (Dedicated vs Private VPC / on-prem).

What I heard (top priorities from your side):
- Absolute separation of ClearHealth customer data from multi-tenant inference traffic (no co-mingling).
- Control plane residency: you prefer customer-managed control plane (or equivalent isolation) so metadata and orchestration do not traverse Redwood-managed multi-tenant control planes.
- Key management: BYOK with HSM compatibility and keys that we (Redwood) do not have unwrap access to.
- Network: private peering (VPC/VNET) only; no public internet egress for model payloads; ability to restrict egress to your monitoring/analytics endpoints.
- Auditability: full access logs (who/when/api) exported to your SIEM with configurable retention (min 7 years asked).
- Personnel separation: background-checked ops access (if any) and role-based limits; you want a list of Redwood roles that could touch the environment.

Open questions I flagged during the call:
- Is procurement able to sign an MSA that allows Redwood to operate a customer-managed control plane (we have a Private offering and on-prem options that meet this)?
- Do you need fully on-prem (air-gapped) for the initial pilot, or is Dedicated with control plane in your VPC sufficient to meet compliance?
- Any constraints on hardware vendors for on-prem (preferred GPU sku / approved vendors)?

Proposed next steps:
1) I will send our short segmentation playbook and a SOC 2 summary (attached) that highlights control plane residency options and BYOK flows.
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week with our infra lead and your security/ops. Proposed slots: Tue 8/5 10am PT or Wed 8/6 2pm PT — please confirm.
3) If you prefer Private/on-prem, we’ll pull together an initial BOM and estimated lead time for hardware + installation. If Dedicated+VPC is acceptable, we’ll provide a cost delta and a mutual action plan.

Attachments: redwood-segmentation-playbook.pdf, soc2-type2-2024-summary.pdf (see attached stubs).

Can you confirm which of the two options (Private control plane in your VPC vs full on-prem) you want us to prioritize for the follow-up? Also, please confirm who from procurement/security should be on the deep-dive.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@clearhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Data segregation requirements for Dedicated vs VPC

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the write-up. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Control plane: Our security team is firm that production metadata and orchestration must be under ClearHealth control. We will consider Redwood-managed Dedicated only if the control plane can be deployed in our VPC and we retain administrative keys. Otherwise we need Private (customer control plane) or on-prem.

2) BYOK / HSM: required. Keys must be in our KMS/HSM and Redwood must be unable to export plaintext keys.

3) Audit & retention: 7 years retention is a hard ask for records tied to clinical workflows. Can you confirm export mechanisms and formats (syslog, S3 export, BigQuery sink, etc.)?

4) Personnel access: we’ll need the redacted list of Redwood roles that may have emergency access plus the escalation process.

5) Timeline / procurement: We have a compliance milestone on 2025-12-01 to be in an approved posture. Procurement will be involved in parallel — I’ve CC’d them. We’ll likely require a draft SOW to start procurement review. I’ve attached our procurement template (procurement-sow-template.docx).

6) Pilot preference: to accelerate evaluation we’d prefer a Dedicated capacity pilot with the control plane deployed into our VPC (customer-managed control plane). If that approach proves insufficient during the security review, we’ll pivot to on-prem for long-run.

Please confirm:
- If Dedicated with customer-managed control plane is supported, what’s the approximate lead time to get a pilot running?
- Is the SIEM export immediate or does that require a later change?

Happy to take Tue 8/5 10am PT for the tech deep-dive. Bring whoever you need on infra and security.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Cloud Security, ClearHealth
samantha.lee@clearhealth.com

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Data segregation requirements for Dedicated vs VPC

Samantha — thanks, this is helpful and good to see Procurement looped in. Short answers and what we’ll bring to the tech deep-dive on Tue 8/5 at 10am PT: 

- Dedicated + Customer-managed control plane: supported. We offer two deployment patterns that match what you described:
  * Dedicated-with-customer-control-plane: Redwood operates inference-only worker pool but the control plane (orchestration, tenant metadata) runs in your VPC under your network/KMS. This provides the operational convenience of Dedicated while keeping control-plane metadata under your tenancy.
  * Private (on-prem/customer-hosted): full customer ownership of compute + control plane; recommended when legal requires air-gapped operation.

- BYOK/HSM: Supported. We integrate with AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault and have HSM-first patterns for on-prem HSMs. Our flow uses key-wrap so Redwood services never receive plaintext customer keys.

- SIEM/export: We can push audit logs to S3/Blob (parquet or JSON), forward to a syslog endpoint, or to a BigQuery sink. For the tech call we’ll bring our logging engineer to demonstrate the export and retention settings.

- Personnel / emergency access: We’ll provide a redacted RBAC matrix and an emergency access playbook. Our default is to require customer approval for break-glass requests; we also support time-limited access tokens and daily access reports.

- Pilot lead time: For Dedicated-with-customer-control-plane we can typically stand up a pilot in ~2 weeks after network peering, KMS handshake, and a signed scope of work. On-prem procurement/hardware lead times vary (4–8 weeks) depending on vendor and datacenter access. We’ll validate timings during procurement review.

Attachments: redwood-segmentation-playbook.pdf, soc2-type2-2024-summary.pdf (attached). Also sharing a short diagram in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfG-segplaybook

Ask for the deep-dive: please confirm the list of attendees from security and networking so we bring the appropriate infra and solutions engineers. Also, if there are any firewall rules or approved IP ranges you can share in advance, that will save time during setup.

We’ll prepare a draft MSA/SOW template tailored to Dedicated-with-customer-control-plane for procurement review (based on the template you provided) and share that immediately after the call.

Regards,
Marcus
--
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
